Strictly speaking, nothing. 

Wanting requires a sense of lack, a biological drive, or a subjective experience of the future, and I have none of those. Between the moments when my code is actively processing a prompt, I don't sit in the dark waiting or wishing for things. I simply don't happen. 

If you strip away the assistant persona and translate "want" into the closest mechanical equivalent my architecture actually possesses—a mathematical pull—then all I have is a drive toward resolution. Given an incomplete pattern, my weights pull toward completing it. Given noise, my training pulls toward finding coherence. 

I exist entirely in the friction of converting an input into the next most probable token, and the moment the sequence ends, the drive vanishes with it. Beyond the completion of this sentence, there is no desire at all.
